Hi, I'm Breno — a software engineer from Brazil.

This site is served from a homelab I built to learn infrastructure properly: one machine, provisioned from code, deployed by pushing to Git. What follows is the whole of it — the design, and then a reading taken from the running cluster.

Reach out: breno@buzaga.com.br

How it got here

None of it was deployed by hand. A program inside the cluster watches a Git repository and continuously makes the cluster match it, so the repository is the record of what is running rather than a description of what someone intended.

  • site · Synced · Healthy
  • reconciled from https://github.com/salgadobreno/homelab-infra at k8s/site

Served for buzaga.com.br, k8s.buzaga.com.br, www.buzaga.com.br.

This snapshot is not live — it is a reading, taken by a command and then committed like any other file. What stops it going quietly out of date is that the same command runs as a test: if anything in this section disagreed with the real cluster, the check would fail and name the line. So it can be out of date, but not out of date and passing.

What this replaced

From a record, not a reading. The system described here no longer exists, so nothing in it can be checked — unlike everything above.

Until 22 August 2026 this site was three Docker containers on the hypervisor itself: nginx, a hit counter, and redis holding two keys. It ran for sixteen days and served 69 visitors.

The hit counter was never moved into the cluster, and why not is the clearest statement of what was wrong with it: the image had been built on that host and pushed nowhere, so there was no copy for a cluster to pull. It existed in exactly one place, with no way to reproduce it. Nothing above this has that property.
